hero.title: It can see what arrived
hero.lede: Customers can attach a photo in the chat. A vision model on your PC reads it, and your flow decides what happens next.

image.alt: Hands opening a cardboard parcel on a table.

tornBox.title: One torn box, from the test day
tornBox.lede: Sam's helmet arrived in a damaged box. The photo is a real stock image and the words are what the models wrote.

items.title: The photo was described
items.text: The Researcher looked at it for 4.5 seconds and wrote down what it saw.

items.title: The order was found
items.text: Order 1270, delivered 13 days earlier. The flow checks for delivery in the last 14 days.

items.title: The limit was checked
items.text: At $150.08 it was under the $300 rule, so nobody had to step in.

items.title: The reply went out
items.text: A free replacement, nothing to send back, and Fernway handles the carrier claim.

customerView.title: What the customer sees
lede: The photo appears in the thread on both sides, so whoever picks it up later has the same picture.

image.alt: The website chat with a photo of a torn box and a reply offering a free replacement.

items.question: How much has this been tested?
items.answer: We tried it with one photo and one flow. Results will vary with your products and how clear the picture is, so keep a limit on what it can approve.

items.question: Is the vision model included?
items.answer: It's an optional download of about 1.8 GB. Qwen3 VL 2B was the one used here.
